about: Threads and GPU kernels in a known schedule. Three named threads pass a baton around a known number of rounds, each holding the cpu for a known time per turn while the other two wait for it; then a fourth thread launches a known number of kernels one at a time and waits for each in a context whose synchronisation blocks.

trust.turns: exact: each lane runs `rounds` turns, one after another in the order of `lanes`, and only one lane is on the cpu at a time
trust.on_cpu: each turn is `turn_s` on the lane's own cpu clock, exact to a few microseconds: each lane is on the cpu `rounds * turn_s`
trust.off_cpu: each lane waits for the other two lanes' turns between its own: at least `(rounds - 1) * 2 * turn_s` blocked, plus the wait before its first turn
trust.switches: a lane leaves the cpu at least once per turn it waits for, so at least `rounds` switches per lane
trust.kernels: exact: `launches` launches of `spin`, one at a time, each waited for; the kernel's duration is the device's, tens of milliseconds for `iterations` on the development machine, not chosen to the microsecond. A machine with no NVIDIA driver runs the threads alone and says so on standard error
trust.wakeups: each turn but the very first begins with the previous lane setting the baton the lane waits on: `rounds` wakeups of each lane by the one before it, less one for `lane-a`, whose first baton is the main thread's
